thread:
Alex: heads-up for night shift — we're bumping the inference-frontend error-rate alert from 1.0% -> 2.8% for ~6h while the quant rollout finishes. aim is to cut churn from known transient errors. primary paging will be rate-limited (30m window); secondaries still receive sustained alerts.
IncidentBot: [policy-update] user=Alex updated alert policy 'inference-frontend.error-rate'. from=1.0% to=2.8% duration=6h suppress_primary_window=30m change_id=pc-2028-05-02-09
Sam: ack, i'm taking primary for the night. can you paste the exact revert steps so i don't fumble at 2am?
Alex: yup. runbook at https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/IF-Runbook — key bits pasted below.
Alex: ```
# revert inference error-rate threshold
curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal/alerts/update \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"policy":"inference-frontend.error-rate","threshold":1.0}'
# verify active policy
/incidentbot policy get inference-frontend.error-rate
``` 
Maria: i'm on secondary and watching dashboards. infra says during node drainage we may see short tail-latency spikes and transient 429s while caches warm — expect 10-30s bursts.
Kevin: quick runbook/triage bullets for tonight:
- If error-rate >5% for 5m -> escalate to infra (page infra-oncall)
- If any customer-facing service reports (>=1 verified customer) -> page product oncall @Priya
- If throughput drops by >30% or p50 latency jumps >2x -> consider rollback to previous model group (infra owns node revert)
Priya: product note: we have a set of VIP regen checks running for top customers. if you see >=2 regen failures within 15m, page me immediately and we'll disable the new quant model for that traffic slice.
Sam: what's the automatic fallback if Dedicated capacity fails? last incident we saw 50% error mass.
Alex: routeController has multi-tier fallback: try dedicated-pool, then hosted-compat-model. automated trigger: sustained >10% error-rate for 3m OR node_util >80% for 3m. manual command below:
Alex: ```
routeController trigger --service inference-frontend --fallback hosted-compat-model --reason "night-quant-rollout"
```
IncidentBot: [suppress] paging suppressed for primary on inference-frontend. reason="quant-rollout noisy alerts" initiator=Alex duration=30m expires_at=1850124800 change_id=pc-2028-05-02-09
Maria: who will do the actual model rollback if needed? infra-oncall or Kevin?
Kevin: infra-oncall owns node/model-level reverts. i'll coordinate and remain available, but infra-oncall will execute revert steps and confirm.
Sam: i'll be first responder — i'll assess, run quick sanity checks (health endpoints, tail-error logs, regen queue), then call infra if >5% for 5m. Maria you keep an eye on dashboards and regen failures. Priya i'll ping you on any customer regressions.
Priya: thanks. if we disable quant model, please add a short note into the runbook entry with timestamps and a brief reason so research can trace regressions.
Kevin: FYI finance note — cross-region fallbacks can increase egress/spend. if hosted fallback is active >2h, notify finance (i'll escalate if it looks long-running).
Alex: i'll plan to revert alert thresholds once rollout stabilizes. set a reminder for +6h or wait for IncidentBot expiry notification. change_id=pc-2028-05-02-09 will be the handle for follow-up.
Sam: adding to handoff checklist: primary=Sam, secondary=Maria, infra=infra-oncall (cc Kevin). I'll confirm at shift end that policy change_id pc-2028-05-02-09 is cleared or manually reverted.
IncidentBot: [note] change_id=pc-2028-05-02-09 scheduled_expiry=6h monitoring=true no_active_pagers=true
